capitals.name: Mangalavada (Mangalvedha)
capitals.note: Bijjala moved his capital from Mangalavada to Kalyani (Bijjala II page); the Kalachuris of Kalyani page says they "made Magaliveda or Mangalavada their capital". The page does not date the move; 1162, when Taila III was driven out of Kalyani, is used.

rulers.name: Bijjala II
rulers.note: the page lists 1130-1167 (he ruled earlier as a Chalukya mahamandalesvara); he "proclaimed independence in 1162" and was assassinated in 1167 (Bijjala II page)

rulers.name: Sankama
rulers.note: Mallugi (no dates) was overthrown by his brother Sankama

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Kalachuri row; its Western Chalukya Empire row, 610,754 km2 in 1165, runs unbroken to 1187). The page: Bijjala "ruled as the Mahamandalesvara (chief or governor) over Karhada-4000 and Tardavadi-1000 provinces" and "assumed imperial titles in 1157"; Taila III still held Kalyani. The two radii are the researcher's reading of Mangalavada and Tardavadi.

"By 1162 CE, Bijjala II had managed to drive Taila III out of Kalyani"; the lead says the Kalachuris "ruled over parts of present-day northern Karnataka and Maharashtra". No area on either page; the radii round Sholapur, Vijayapura, Bidar, Belagavi and Raichur are the researcher's reading. The Western Chalukyas "gradually retrieved the territory" after 1181.

notes: Cliopatria has no Kalachuri row and its Western Chalukya Empire row runs unbroken to 1187, so a compiler must decide the 1162-1184 overlap: this dossier says the Kalyani heartland was Kalachuri, and the Western Chalukya dossier should show the loss in 1162 and the recovery 1181-1184 (page silent on the exact years). The ruler list and the 1181 infobox end disagree; 1184 follows the list. Gazetteer lacks Kalyani (Basavakalyan), Mangalavada, Karhada, Tardavadi; radii around Sholapur, Vijayapura, Bidar, Belagavi and Raichur stand in.
